full_judgment: 115. Reverting back to the case in hand, it is stated in the FIR that dates of occurrences are between the periods from 26-6-2012 to 24-7-2019. The FIR was lodged on 9-12-2019. It is further stated in the FIR that following negotiations between the parties (more specifically, according to the charge-sheet, in November, 2011 and in February, 2012 two meetings were held regarding the matter between the parties in which the stakeholders of both companies were present), the informant gave Taka twenty crore to the accused between 26-6-2012 to 16-4-2016 as loan under two contracts for setting up sweater factory by the accused and to import machineries for the factory through the company of the informant. However, the informant continued to disburse loan to the accused which in total stood at Taka ninety five crore. Then, another contract was executed under which the accused promised to repay the loan within 3 (three) years and he, in fact, repaid Taka two crore twenty lac. Thereafter, accounts were settled and on 22-7-2017 a MoU was executed between the parties in respect of repayment of the outstanding loan amount, but the accused did not repay the loan money. There is no allegation, whatsoever, either in the FIR or in the charge-sheet that the accused did not set up the factory or that he did not import machineries through the informant's company. It has been stated in the charge-sheet (not in the FIR) that at one stage, the informant came to know that after receipt of the loan money, the accused purchased land using the loan money instead of utilizing the same properly under the terms of the contract. It is further stated in the charge-sheet that in spite of such knowledge the informant continued to give cash loan to the accused. Considering the principles laid down in the decided cases, it can be safely concluded that in the instant case there was no initial intention to deceive the informant and that the transactions between the parties, which arose out of several contracts, are purely of civil nature and do not attract any criminal liability. It is interesting to note that there is no allegation, whatsoever, in the FIR that the accused refused to repay the loan money, rather it is stated in the FIR that from the conduct of the accused, the informant was confirmed that the accused had deceived him and misappropriated the money. Suffice it say that law will take its course on facts, not on the presumption of the complainant. Facts stated in the FIR and in the charge-sheet do not attract the definition of criminal intimidation given in section 503 of the Penal Code.
